articles.title: Patna HC cautions DMs, SPs against misuse of crime control law
articles.summary: Patna High Court quashes three externment orders, warns DMs/SPs on misuse of Bihar crime-control laws, and imposes Rs 3.9 lakh cost on state as compensation.
articles.body: By: Dev Kumar PandeyPATNA: The Patna high court has cautioned district magistrates (DMs) and superintendents of police (SPs) against declaring people “antisocial” without strictly following procedural norms, while imposing a total cost of Rs3.9 lakh on the state govt in three cases involving externment orders under Bihar’s crime control law.A division bench of Justices Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Sunil Dutta Mishra passed the three orders on Sept 11 while quashing externment orders challenged through separate criminal writ petitions. The orders came into the public domain on Sept 12.In a petition filed by Chandan Kumar, an elected panchayati raj representative from Giriyak block in Nalanda district, the court quashed an externment order passed by the Nalanda DM. It directed Kumar to mark his attendance at Silao police station every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.The court imposed a cost of Rs60,000 on the state in the case as compensation to Kumar.In another petition filed by Shashi Kumar alias Fukan and Ajay Singh, both residents of a village under Katrisarai police station area in Nalanda, the court quashed an externment order dated Oct 10, 2025, passed by the Nalanda DM, holding that it amounted to an abuse of the provisions of the Bihar crime control law.The court imposed a cost of Rs2.2 lakh, or Rs 1.1 lakh each, as compensation to the two petitioners.The bench criticised the roles of the Nalanda SP and DM, describing the former as “acting as a post office” and the latter as “acting as a drastic power house” while declaring persons accused of minor offences as “antisocial”.The third case involved Girdhari Yadav, a resident of Katoria police station area in Banka district. The court found fault with an externment order dated Sept 8, 2025, passed by the Banka DM, under which Yadav had been directed to mark his daily attendance at Barahat police station, around 40km from his village.The court quashed the order and imposed a cost of Rs1.1 lakh on the state as compensation to Yadav.The bench directed the state govt to pay the compensation awarded to all four petitioners within a month and recover the amount from the officers found responsible.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: ‘May have to go back to cash’: Traders on UPI MDR
articles.summary: Delhi traders warn they may revert to cash after govt imposes 0.4% MDR on UPI payments above Rs 2,000; small merchants get exemption, MDR can’t be passed on.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “We may have to go back to cash” – this is the refrain at Delhi’s markets after Centre introduced a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.Traders and shopkeepers said they may stop accepting digital payments for larger transactions if they have to bear the additional cost.For businesses that have spent years shifting customers from cash to UPI, the move has come as a setback. They questioned why they should bear another transaction-related cost after paying GST and other business expenses. Some, they said, may now encourage customers to pay in cash.“We were already paying transaction charges and 18% GST. Now if govt charges us on UPI MDR, then we will promote cash. When govt came with the UPI payment method, we supported it. We are already grappling with issues like freezing of bank accounts and the imposition of restrictions due to complaints regarding cyber fraud. In such a climate, any additional increase in the cost of accepting digital payments is a cause for concern for small and medium-sized traders,” said Kamla Nagar Market Association president Nitin Gupta.“We have got used to digital payments. Sometimes, when we go to the market, we don’t even carry cash. It will be tough for us to go back to cash payments,” he added.Govt announced the charge Tuesday as part of a framework for large digital merchant payments, ending the zero-MDR regime that has been in place since Jan 2020.Traders and shop owners in several markets, including Kalkaji, Kamla Nagar, Khan Market, Laxmi Nagar and Sadar Bazar, said the decision has created confusion over who will bear the additional cost.They said even if the charge is not directly recovered from customers, it would add to the cost of doing business and could squeeze already limited margins.At Shree Shyam Jewellers in Kalkaji’s Block A, a shopkeeper said, “There is already so much confusion. After paying taxes, 18% GST and meeting so many other business expenses, an additional transaction charge is simply unacceptable. It will put another burden on us. We cannot keep absorbing costs,” he said.Brijesh Goel, chairperson of Chamber of Trade and Industry, said the move could encourage a shift towards cash transactions.“In the past six years, we have with great difficulty brought even the smallest of shopkeepers and street vendors onto UPI. Today, 90% of payments in Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Chawri Bazar, Kamla Nagar, Karol Bagh and Gandhi Nagar are through UPI. If MDR is imposed, it will be a setback to the Digital India mission,” he said.New Delhi Traders Association general secretary Amit Gupta said traders had no objection to digital payments but are opposed to the additional cost.“UPI was introduced to make digital payments easier for both traders and customers. If traders are now asked to bear an additional charge on transactions above Rs 2,000, many of them will prefer cash payment,” he said.Sadar Bazar Bari Market Traders Association president Paramjit Singh Pamma said the impact could be significant for businesses handling hundreds of large UPI transactions.“Profit margins are already limited, especially for small and medium-sized merchants. If merchants are charged for every large digital payment, it will directly impact their savings and profits,” Pamma said.The framework provides an exemption for small merchants earning up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes, with govt saying this covers 96% of merchant transactions.The MDR cannot be passed on to customers, while person-to-person UPI transfers remain outside the charge.Essential sectors such as railways, telecom and fuel will attract a flat Rs 5 fee per transaction, while capital market transactions will have a 0.02% rate.Petrol pump dealers, meanwhile, said they were waiting for clarity from the ministry of petroleum before deciding how to respond.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 6 years on, gangster Vikas Dubey is officially dead
articles.summary: Kanpur Nagar Nigam issues Vikas Dubey death certificate six years after 2020 encounter, after High Court probe over wrong father’s name blocked insurance and property transfer.
articles.body: KANPUR: Kanpur Nagar Nigam issued the death certificate of gangster Vikas Dubey, the main accused in the Bikru case, on Sept 11, about six years after he was killed in a police encounter.Dubey died in Kanpur on July 10, 2020, but his death certificate could not be issued because his father’s name was incorrectly recorded in the panchnama and cremation slip. Instead of Ram Kumar Dubey, his father’s name was entered as Raj Kumar Dubey.His wife, Richa Dubey, approached several officials before filing a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking the certificate. Following directions from the High Court, the health department investigated the matter.Chief medical officer Dr Hari Dutt Nemi visited the post-mortem house as part of the inquiry, after which the certificate was issued.Nagar Nigam sources said the certificate was sent by registered post to the Bikru address provided by the court. It was widely circulated on social media after reaching the village.Richa told the court that Dubey was not considered dead in the official records, preventing the nominee from receiving benefits under an insurance policy in his name. His property and land could also not be transferred to his heirs.On July 2, 2020, a police team went to Bikru village in Chaubepur police station area to arrest Dubey. Its vehicles were blocked with a JCB, and gunmen opened fire from rooftops as personnel approached his house.Eight policemen, including a circle officer, were killed. UP police and Special Task Force subsequently killed six criminals linked to the case in encounters.Rajesh Singh, zonal officer of Zone 4, Nagar Nigam, confirmed on Wednesday that the certificate had been issued and sent by registered post.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kanpur | Silver Rate in Kanpur | Bank Holidays in Kanpur | Public Holidays in Kanpur | Kanpur AQI | Weather in Kanpur | Petrol Price in Kanpur | Diesel Price in Kanpur | CNG Price in Kanpur | LPG Price in KanpurStay updated with the latest Kanpur news. articles.title: Days after PM Modi’s school friend gets relief in land dispute, Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancels construction permission to BJP MLA’s company
articles.summary: Mira-Bhayander civic body cancels building permission for BJP MLA Narendra Mehta’s firm Seven Eleven amid land dispute; tehsildar rules for Asgarali Vohra.
articles.body: BHAYANDER: The Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation on Wednesday cancelled the construction permission granted to Seven Eleven company, days after BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land following the matter being taken up with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven and other respondents. The order is expected to clear the way for Vohra’s name to be entered in the land records for the property currently in the possession of Seven Eleven, which had fenced off the plot with metal sheets.Vohra had alleged that Mehta and Swayam Builders had illegally encroached on the land at Navghar in Bhayander. He had been pursuing the dispute for around 15 years.On September 8, Vohra approached PM Modi, whom he described as his childhood friend from B N School in Vadnagar in Gujarat, and sought his intervention in the dispute. Soon after, Mehta announced that he would relinquish possession of the property and withdraw a complaint filed against Vohra.On Wednesday, Mehta issued a statement denying that he or his company had cheated anyone. He said the disputed land had been sold to Vohra in 1989 by Renol Lobo and five others. Lobo and the others later sold the land to Swayam Builders in 2011, he said.Mehta further claimed that Seven Eleven had purchased the property through duly registered transactions from Joseph Fernandes and Mukesh Parekh. He said the company decided to return the land to Mukesh Parekh and Mervin Fernandes after a dispute arose over the property.The BJP MLA maintained that surrendering possession and cancelling the transaction was a decision taken to end the dispute and did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Time-bound entry and exit plan for private vehicles at Pune airport awaited a year after announcement
articles.summary: Pune airport’s time-bound entry/exit plan for private vehicles remains unimplemented nearly a year on, amid congestion complaints; authorities say rollout is pending.
articles.body: PUNE: Almost a year after Pune airport authorities announced a time-bound entry and exit system for private vehicles, it is yet to be implemented.Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke told TOI that the plan was in its final stages, but officials were still working out the implementation mechanism to ensure passenger convenience. “Some discussions have been underway on how to effectively implement it so that flyers were not left in the lurch. Once we have found a proper way of implementation, it will start,” Dhoke said.He was talking on the sidelines of the announcement of the launch of ‘Yatri Seva Abhiyan’, a pan-India passenger-centric campaign from Sept 17 to Oct 10, 2026, organised by the Airports Authority of India (AAI).The delay in implementation has drawn criticism from frequent flyers. They said haphazardly parked vehicles outside the terminal obstructed the traffic and the airport shuttle movement, particularly during late evening and night hours.Ashish Sankule, a Ganeshkhind Road resident and regular flyer, said the airport needed to take a stricter approach towards vehicles blocking the arrival area. “Why was it taking so long for the airport authorities to implement this? It should have been simple – fine vehicles that block the pathway. There would always be people who protest, but the airport authorities needed to be strict,” he said.He said he had witnessed instances when shuttle buses operating between the airport and AeroMall struggled to move because of vehicles parked indiscriminately. “Those who follow the rules and park their vehicles at AeroMall end up finding it difficult to reach passengers waiting at the airport,” he said.Discussions on the time-bound system have been underway since last year. In Feb, airport authorities had said private vehicles would be given a maximum waiting window of 13-15 minutes to enter the airport, pick up passengers and exit. Vehicles exceeding the stipulated time were proposed to be penalised with hefty fines.Another frequent flyer and Koregaon Park resident, Shekhar Sinha, said implementation was necessary, but authorities also needed to address parking on the roads surrounding the airport.“Not just cabs, but private vehicles have been parked everywhere in the vicinity of the airport because people did not want to use AeroMall and pay parking fees. This was causing congestion on Airport Road and New Airport Road, but authorities did not seem to care,” he said.Sinha said airport authorities should implement the time-bound entry system immediately while coordinating with traffic police to tackle roadside parking. “If we have been talking about a ‘Yatri Seva Abhiyan’, these problems also need to be addressed,” he said.Dhoke said the transfer of 13 acres of defence land to the AAI, pending for nearly two years, was expected shortly. He said the required infrastructure has been completed for the Indian Air Force in lieu of the land. “The same was with the Defence Estate Office, and we should get it very soon. Once we get it, a plan would be drawn on what kind of expansion can be undertaken on the land as part of the masterplan,” Dhoke told TOI.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: 900m buffer zone earmarked in Gurgaon, but not even 9m gap between houses and IAF ammo depot
articles.summary: Gurgaon’s 900m buffer around an IAF ammo depot is densely encroached, with 15 illegal colonies and 5,000+ structures; SC questions officials’ collusion.
articles.body: GURGAON: The 900-metre restricted zone around Indian Air Force’s ammunition depot in old Gurgaon has been almost entirely built over, with multi-storey houses standing virtually flush against the facility’s boundary wall, leaving little to no buffer between habitation and a sensitive defence installation.Supreme Court on Tuesday criticised state officials for colluding with local land sharks to allow this encroachment. The depot was established in 1947.Fifteen illegal colonies have come up in the belt over the years, turning it into a dense urban pocket of kothis built cheek by jowl along narrow lanes.Residential buildings, PG accommodations, shops, schools, factories, cloud kitchens and commercial establishments now fill the zone. In several stretches, no open space separates the built-up area from the depot wall.Five- to seven-storey buildings have come up close to the installation, giving occupants elevated vantage points overlooking the depot — effectively erasing the physical buffer the restricted zone was meant to preserve.The affected pockets include Sheetla Colony, Rajiv Nagar, Sanjay Gram, Sukhrali Enclave, Ashok Vihar Phase 3, Om Vihar, Dharam Colony, Amanpura and Caterpuri, among others. The 900-metre zone covers roughly 2,325 acres.During Tuesday’s hearing, CJI Surya Kant said the no-go zone was earlier more than a kilometre and it gradually reduced to 900 metres, and even then, the illegal constructions were carried out right under the nose of the officials. “Are the encroachments not because of the collusion of govt officials with the land mafia,” he asked.Surveys and govt reports put the numbers differently. An MCG survey in 2017 identified 4,156 illegal structures within this belt. Officials estimate the number has since roughly doubled.Older govt data, including in the submissions made to the high court, had put total structures at 14,154, while a more recent MCG report flagged over 5,000 unauthorised structures and more than 190 ongoing construction sites in the zone.Punjab and Haryana high court had previously held that the 900-metre strip must remain free of urbanisation, and found that authorities allowed illegal construction to proliferate there. The court described the depot as a strategic installation where national interest could not be compromised.But govt action has repeatedly cut against this position. In 2015, Haryana filed an affidavit before the high court seeking to reduce the restricted zone from 900 to 300 metres.In 2016, the urban local bodies department approved temporary water connections for families in the 900-metre zone, citing the difficulty of removing thousands of residents.In 2017, authorities were directed to clear encroachments within a tighter 300-metre radius. A subsequent survey found 3,346 structures there, and the high court ordered their removal.MCG sealed several under-construction buildings last month, but a follow-up visit found many had been de-sealed and construction resumed. Hundreds of buildings are currently under construction in the zone.Residents describe a parallel civic ecosystem that has grown alongside the illegal settlement. A Sheetla Colony resident of about a decade alleged that local politicians and officials encouraged poor families to invest in construction there. “They help residents get voter cards and then use them as a vote bank during elections,” he said.A woman living in the area said residents have long been promised regularisation. “They help us get water and electricity connections. Roads have been built and sewerage laid,” she said.Another resident alleged that development tenders issued for adjoining areas are, in practice, executed inside the restricted zone: “Tenders are issued for development work in adjoining areas, but the actual work is carried out inside the 900-metre zone,” this person said.The issue has remained politically live. During the 2024 assembly campaign, Gurgaon MLA Mukesh Sharma listed resolving the zone’s problems among his priorities.In June 2026, Sharma met defence minister Rajnath Singh to seek the Centre’s intervention, citing the impact of the restrictions on civic works, property registrations and statutory approvals in the affected localities.A similar situation has played out near Faridabad Air Force Station in Dabua, where illegal construction within the restricted zone has been before Punjab and Haryana high court for over 15 years.The Centre notified a 100-metre restricted belt around the station in Jan 2010 under Works of Defence Act, prohibiting construction in the area. The matter reached the high court the same year through petitions seeking removal of illegal structures and action against officials responsible.In 2012, the court directed Faridabad Municipal Corporation to act against the illegal structures. By 2017, authorities estimated around 5,000 houses could be affected, and a 2018 survey identified 2,717 buildings within the 100-metre belt.Notices were issued to occupants, and authorities were directed to prevent further construction and transactions, but large populated colonies remain, with the issue still mired in legal and administrative hurdles.An area originally meant to stay free of urbanisation to protect a defence installation has become one of the city’s most densely populated pockets — serviced, in part, by the same civic machinery meant to keep it clear.With construction still underway, the unresolved question is not how the colonies came up, but how thousands of structures have been allowed to remain, expand and receive civic infrastructure inside a decades-old security zone.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: DUSU elections: ABVP, NSUI trade allegations of attacks and intimidation ahead of polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With Delhi University set to vote for its students’ union on September 18, the ABVP and National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) have trade.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With Delhi University set to vote for its students’ union on September 18, the ABVP and National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) have traded allegations of attacks and intimidation involving their members and candidates, with both student organisations demanding police action.In a press statement, the ABVP alleged that NSUI workers entered the residence of its members at Hari Mandir in Delhi and attacked them while they were holding a meeting.It said women student members were also present at the residence when the alleged incident took place.The ABVP alleged that several individuals fled the spot after the alleged attack, while one person was apprehended by its members and handed over to the police. It further claimed that the apprehended person admitted to being part of NSUI’s social media cadre.ABVP Delhi State secretary Sarthak Sharma said, "NSUI must explain why its workers reached the residence of ABVP members and attacked them despite women student activists being present there. ABVP members were holding a peaceful meeting and had not provoked anyone. One person who was fleeing after the attack was apprehended and handed over to the police. ABVP did not take the law into its own hands; instead, we handed the individual over to the police.""The apprehended person has admitted to being part of NSUI's social media cadre. Congress-IYC-NSUI must explain why its social media cadre was involved in an attack on the residence of ABVP members? Students of Delhi University can clearly see the difference between democratic student engagement and the use of violence. ABVP members are continuously engaging with students peacefully, while people associated with Congress-IYC-NSUI are allegedly resorting to violence," he alleged.Sharma further noted, "The Congress leadership must clarify its political accountability for the activities of its youth and student organisations. ABVP will not be intimidated by violence or pressure. We demand an impartial police investigation and strict legal action against all those involved, along with adequate measures to ensure the safety of students. The facts of the incident can also be verified from the local police."The NSUI, meanwhile, alleged that ABVP workers attacked the residences of its DUSU candidates Vijay Shankar Meena and Gopal Choudhary. It alleged that nearly 200 ABVP workers were involved in targeting and intimidating its candidates.NSUI Media Incharge Ravi Pandey said, "This is a desperate attempt to create fear and violence just before the DUSU elections. We demand immediate intervention and strict action by the Delhi Police to ensure the safety of our candidates and students. Such hooliganism cannot be allowed in a democratic student election.""ABVP knows that students are ready for change. On September 18, Delhi University students will answer this politics of intimidation through their democratic vote," he added.The NSUI, in its statement, appealed to the Delhi Police and university authorities to take immediate steps to ensure peace and security during the election process.The allegations come amid heightened tensions on the Delhi University campus in the run-up to the DUSU polls.On the final day of campaigning, separate clashes and allegations of violence were reported at multiple locations, with ABVP and NSUI also trading accusations over some of those incidents.(With ANI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Kash defends FBI hiring rule shift on bestiality: 'Won't target victims'
articles.summary: US News: WASHINGTON: FBI director Kash Patel defended Tuesday a recent policy change to allow some applicants who have engaged in prostitution and bestiality t.
articles.body: WASHINGTON: FBI director Kash Patel defended Tuesday a recent policy change to allow some applicants who have engaged in prostitution and bestiality to be considered for employment, insisting that the move was made to enable victims of those acts to apply for a job without fear of automatic disqualification.The subject arose during a fiery senate judiciary committee hearing. Under questioning, Patel denied that the changes reflected a lowering of employment standards and insisted they were designed to prevent victims who'd been forced to engage in that conduct from being automatically disqualified."We did not want to punish victims of bestiality, victims who were trafficked. We did not want to make it an automatic disqualification for the FBI to consider you if you were a victim of these awful, heinous acts," the FBI director said. "We are not going to target victims and prevent them from serving in their capacity to serve this country."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Maratha activist Jarange Patil calls off 20-day fast, gives govt 3 months to consider demands
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government th.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands, news agency PTI reported.The decision came after Jarange addressed a large gathering at Patoda in Beed district around 2 am, raising concerns about his worsening physical condition and the possibility of abandoning his planned march to Mumbai.Jarange, who had entered the day 18 of his fast at the time of the address, said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him.He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at Khopoli. He warned that if the convoy continued, he might stop the journey and resume his sit-in protest in Patoda or return to Antarwali Sarati.Despite reaching the venue at around 1.30 am, Jarange found thousands of people, including women, waiting to hear him speak.Addressing the gathering, he said he could barely move his limbs after stopping IV fluids on September 12."Fighting for the children of my community has taken a toll on my body, but I have taken on the government for you. The government wants me to surrender, but should I abandon our demand? My community is greater than any government - it is my father. My community holds the power to bring down any government and install a new one," he asserted.Jarange said the movement had made progress after 58 lakh archival records, known as nondi, were uncovered. He claimed these records could help nearly 2.5 crore members of the Maratha community access reservation benefits.He said the immediate demand was for the Maharashtra government to issue an official gazette recognising the relevant records.The activist also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, claiming he had countered the government's political moves and that all the documented records had been secured on pen drives. He further accused Fadnavis of "plotting against his life".Responding to the government's argument about fruit orchard owners in Western Maharashtra, Jarange questioned why OBC communities that also own orchards should not receive reservation benefits."The government claims Western Maharashtra has fruit orchards, but don't OBC communities own orchards too? Why do they have a reservation then?"Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He appealed to supporters to avoid following his vehicle and said he would prefer to travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda after speaking to the police, if his health allowed.He also spoke about his family, saying he had asked them to live with self-respect and told his son to remain courageous if he died for the community."I have told my family to live with self-respect. I told my son to step up courageously if I give my life for the community. Let one life be sacrificed for the cause, but never let the dignity of our caste be lowered," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BLA claims killing 43 Pakistan military personnel past week
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week, saying its fighters killed 4.
articles.body: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week, saying its fighters killed 43 Pakistani military and state-affiliated "Death Squad" personnel. The rebel group acknowledged losing 10 fighters.BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the operations, involving road blockades, targeted strikes, took place in Besima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Surab, Qila Abdullah and Awaran, where it claimed two Pakistani army soldiers were killed.According to the statement, BLA said it imposed multi-hour blockades on Besima-Kapuk and Quetta-Taftan trade routes to conduct snap checks and restrict troop movements. It claimed 25 personnel were killed on Sept 13 in an ambush on state-aligned local militias in Sultan Charak, Qila Abdullah, followed by a four-hour clash with army reinforcements.The group also claimed its "Fateh Squad" killed nine soldiers in Lasbela, while another operation targeted four military intelligence operatives in Jiwani. It said fighters destroyed surveillance equipment in Panjgur and burnt machinery at a lithium extraction site in Machil under its "economic blockade". BLA said it would continue armed resistance until Pakistani security forces withdrew from the region entirely. On Monday, it released a video purportedly showing fighters seizing 14 posts on Quetta-Taftan Highway.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: AT&T CEO John Stankey, as part of our company's culture we have a principle for all meetings: Do not walk into a meeting without ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: AT&T CEO John Stankey has laid out a clear cultural principle for his company that employees should never walk into a meeting unprepared. Accordin.
articles.body: AT&T CEO John Stankey has laid out a clear cultural principle for his company that employees should never walk into a meeting unprepared. According to a report by Fortune, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, hosted by LinkedIN, Stankey emphasised that success requires discourse, data-driven perspectives, and the courage to speak up. Stankey said one of AT&T’s guiding principles is that employees must come to meetings ready to contribute. “Don’t walk in there and just be an observer,” he explained. “When you have a point of view, it shouldn’t just be some uninformed opinion. It should be a point of view that’s built on facts, information, and data. I crave that.”He added that if participants aren’t willing to share constructive insights, it may mean the wrong people are in the room. The approach is designed to avoid groupthink and ensure meetings are productive rather than ceremonial.JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon’s perspectiveJamie Dimon echoed Stankey’s sentiment, noting that leaders must create environments where employees feel comfortable disagreeing or raising uncomfortable issues. “I am never upset when someone says I’m wrong about something,” Dimon said. “I just want to do the best I can for our clients, our country, our company.”Dimon has long stressed the importance of preparation, saying he always does pre-reads before meetings and believes in eliminating unnecessary meetings altogether.Meeting prep in the age of AIThe conversation also touched on how both executives are adjusting their meeting preparation habits as AI tools become part of their daily workflow. Both have traditionally stressed the value of reading materials ahead of meetings, but they suggested that habit may be shifting. Stankey said he's begun questioning whether reading is still the most effective way to absorb information, noting that engaging in a more conversational, dialogue-based format with AI now lets him process information faster when the conversation is well-directed. Dimon said he takes a similar approach, using AI tools like Gemini or Google to quickly dig into information as part of his meeting previews.Even so, the core principle hasn't changed for either executive: showing up prepared remains essential. Early in his career, as a 28-year-old Harvard MBA working as an assistant to American Express president Sanford "Sandy" Weill, Dimon saw his role as primarily learning and observing, holding off on speaking until he had something valuable to contribute.That instinct to stay quiet and absorb information, however, likely wouldn't hold up well in Stankey's meeting culture — where a young employee following Dimon's old playbook might instead find themselves cold-called and expected to offer a point of view on the spot.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: A tech entrepreneur paid £555,000 for a derelict Welsh island fort; after a nearly five-year restoration, it is on the market for £3 million
articles.summary: UK News: A derelict 19th-century fortress sitting on a tiny island off the Pembrokeshire coast had no electricity, no running water and had been empty for 17 y.
articles.body: A derelict 19th-century fortress sitting on a tiny island off the Pembrokeshire coast had no electricity, no running water and had been empty for 17 years when technology entrepreneur Mike Conner bought it in 2017. He paid £555,000 for Thorne Island and then spent almost five years bringing the abandoned fort back to life. It now has 40 beds, four en-suite bathrooms and its own nightclub, and has been put back on the market for £3 million.How a 1850s Welsh island fort went from military base to abandoned ruinAccording to the data cited on island’s official site, Thorne Island lies near Milford Haven in Pembrokeshire and was originally built in the 1850s to protect the important naval port from French attacks. The 100-man fort later had a very different life, becoming a hotel in 1947 and hosting weddings, birthdays and stag parties.It was eventually sold in 1999, but attempts to bring it back into use failed. The island changed hands twice more in the years that followed, including a stint with a hotel group that abandoned plans for a costly relaunch, before Conner bought the listed building in May 2017, by which point it had sat largely derelict and overgrown for close to two decades.The first challenge was simply getting waterThe fort was a long way from being a functioning home when Conner arrived. There was no electricity or running water, while food and waste had to be transported between the island and the mainland.Even installing a working toilet became a major engineering job. According to the BBC, Conner had to cut through about 16ft (5m) of rock to reach a biodigester pump, a process that ultimately cost about £200,000.The restoration eventually took nearly five years, with six men living on the island for around four years while the work was carried out. Much of the equipment needed for the project had to be transported by helicopter because of the island's difficult location.The abandoned fort became a party spaceThe finished Thorne Island is very different from the waterlogged, empty building Conner purchased. The restored property now has 40 beds, four en-suite bathrooms and a nightclub, with the old military fort adapted for large gatherings and private events.The island had already developed a reputation as a party venue during its years as a hotel. Conner has continued that tradition, hosting events there himself, including celebrations for his 50th birthday. The island can accommodate around 800 people for events, although its current configuration provides sleeping space for about 40.Thorne Island is now on the market for £3 millionAfter years spent restoring the fort, Conner has decided to sell the unusual property. It is now being offered for £3 million, giving a new owner the chance to take over a private island with a restored historic fortress and facilities designed for large-scale entertainment.Conner told the BBC that he sees several possible futures for the site, from a tourist attraction to an events venue. He said the island could host what he described as an “unbelievable 24-hour experience”, with its isolation making it possible to hold large events without nearby neighbours.For Conner, the project was also more personal than simply renovating a property. He discovered during the restoration that he is a quarter Welsh, as his mother grew up at Upton Castle near Pembroke Dock. After years of construction, helicopter deliveries and engineering problems, the former technology entrepreneur now hopes someone else will decide what the unusual Welsh fortress becomes next.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ICE agent accused of shooting Venezuelan man arrested after 8 months
articles.summary: US News: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man was arrested in Minneapolis on Wednesday. The detention comes .
articles.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man was arrested in Minneapolis on Wednesday. The detention comes eight months after the incident in which he wounded the man and later lied to investigators, which became a flashpoint in US President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.Christian Castro turned himself in to agents of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension in downtown Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin County jail on an outstanding arrest warrant, ICE said.Castro is facing state assault charges over the January 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan national. He is also accused of falsely reporting a crime after allegedly telling Department of Homeland Security officials that Sosa-Celis and others had attacked him with a snow shovel and broom. Video evidence later disproved that account, prosecutors said.Castro's arrest came after he was released on bond from federal custody earlier this month. He had been arrested in Texas on separate federal charges of making false statements to investigators about the shooting and was released with a GPS ankle monitor.His lawyer, Rolando Cantu, said Castro had always intended to face the charges in Minneapolis. He disputed prosecutors' claims that his client might flee to Mexico."He wants his day in court."Castro was expected to make his first state court appearance in Minneapolis on Thursday. He is due to appear in US District Court in neighbouring St Paul on Friday morning over the federal charges.Case linked to Operation Metro SurgeThe state case stems from a confrontation during Operation Metro Surge, the large-scale ICE deployment in Minneapolis as part of Trump's wider immigration crackdown.Castro allegedly shot Sosa-Celis in the leg through the door of his apartment while children were inside. The incident triggered protests and clashes between federal immigration agents and demonstrators.After the shooting, Castro returned to his home state of Texas, preventing Minnesota authorities from immediately arresting him. A warrant was later issued for his arrest.Texas Rangers eventually apprehended Castro. However, Texas Governor Greg Abbott declined to sign extradition papers sent by Minnesota Governor Tim Walz.Abbott questioned whether Castro could be considered a fugitive because the Department of Homeland Security had reassigned him to Texas after the Minneapolis shooting.Castro spent about 90 days in a Texas county jail and was released on August 27 after a federal judge rejected Minnesota's request for an immediate extradition order.He was arrested again in Texas after a federal grand jury indicted him in early September on charges of making false statements. The indictment marked the first US Justice Department prosecution of a federal law enforcement officer accused of wrongdoing linked to Operation Metro Surge.DHS has suspended Castro from ICE. A person familiar with the case has also said that a civil rights investigation into the shooting of Sosa-Celis was opened."Governor Abbott’s attempt to shield Mr. Castro from accountability has failed. We look forward to commencing our prosecution," Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said in a statement.

articles.title: MDR charges explained: Who will pay how much for UPI?
articles.summary: Money Matters News: From October 15, some UPI payments will stop being free for the people who receive them. The rules come from two places. On September 14, the Finance .
articles.body: From October 15, some UPI payments will stop being free for the people who receive them. The rules come from two places. On September 14, the Finance Ministry issued a notification under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. It kept UPI payments of up to Rs 2,000, and RuPay debit cards, free of any bank or system charge. A day later, the steering committee led by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) announced what happens above that line.Much of the reaction has been noise, so the details are worth setting out first.Who pays, and how muchThe charge is a merchant discount rate, or MDR. It is the fee a business pays for accepting a digital payment, and it is common with cards. For UPI, it will be 0.4 per cent on person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above Rs 2,000.In practice:PaymentCharge to the merchantRs 1,500 to a shopNilRs 2000 to a shopNilRs 3000 to a shopRs 12Rs 10,000 to a shopRs 40Rs 50,000 to a retailerRs 200Rs 75,000 or moreRs 300 (cap)On a Rs 1 lakh purchase, 0.4 per cent would be Rs 400, but the cap keeps it at Rs 300.Several things do not change:Transfers between individuals remain free at any amount. Sending Rs 20,000 to a friend costs nothing.Small merchants are protected. Those in the P2PM category, receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through QR payments into their own accounts, pay nothing, even on a single payment above Rs 2,000. They move into the regular category only if they cross that limit for three consecutive months.AutoPay mandates for subscriptions, EMIs, insurance premiums and utility bills carry no prescribed MDR.Some sectors pay a flat Rs 5 on payments above Rs 2,000. These are railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and public utilities. A Rs 20,000 railway booking costs Rs 5, not Rs 80.Capital-market payments, to mutual funds, brokers and investment platforms, attract 0.02 per cent, also capped at Rs 300.The customer is not supposed to pay any of this. The government says banks have been told to ensure merchants do not pass the charge on, and that UPI apps cannot add platform fees. On paper, UPI stays free for the consumer.The case for the feeThe government's reasoning is not frivolous. UPI now handles about 2,400 crore transactions a month, worth close to Rs 30 lakh crore. A system that size needs constant spending on servers, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, dispute resolution and resilience. Since 2020, the basic merchant payment has earned banks and apps almost nothing, and subsidies have covered part of the gap. NPCI says the new revenue will stay within the ecosystem.The Rs 2,000 line was chosen with care. More than 95 per cent of UPI merchant payments are at or below it, so the tea stall and the kirana shop are untouched. The fee falls on larger commercial payments.So why the uproar over a charge this small?Small charges rarely stay smallThe first reason is precedent. The Securities Transaction Tax was introduced in 2004 alongside the removal of long-term capital gains tax on listed shares. In 2018, the capital gains tax returned. The STT stayed. Dividends, once taxed at the company level, are now taxed in shareholders' hands at slab rates. The concern is not today's Rs 40. It is that once a charging mechanism exists, the rate, the cap and the threshold can all change without much public debate.The second is pass-through. The rule says merchants should not add the fee to the bill, but merchants set their own prices. Anyone who has been told "2 per cent extra on card" knows how quickly such costs reach the customer. Retail prices are also rounded, so a Rs 20 cost can turn into a Rs 30 or Rs 50 increase. Once the charge disappears into the price, it becomes harder to see, and cash buyers end up paying it too.The third is cash. Some shopkeepers will offer a discount for cash rather than give up 0.4 per cent. Reports from Delhi suggest some traders have already started. For jewellers, furniture showrooms, contractors and clinics, that is an easy trade. It works directly against the formalisation that UPI has done so much to advance.The fourth is the threshold itself. A Rs 1,999 payment is free and a Rs 2,001 payment is not. A Rs 5,000 bill can become Rs 2,000, Rs 2,000 and Rs 1,000. The system will need monitoring to stop this, which brings its own cost.The fifth is how the numbers are presented. "Over 95 per cent of transactions stay free" counts payments, not money. Industry estimates suggest payments above Rs 2,000 make up about 4 per cent of merchant volume but roughly two-thirds of its value. Those larger payments are also where a digital trail matters most for tax.A rate that does not fit investingThe capital-market rate needs a second look. Money sent to a broker does not have to result in a trade, and the broker cannot pass the fee to the client. Consider 10,000 customers each making 50 transfers of Rs 2 lakh in a month without trading. At 0.02 per cent, that costs the broker about Rs 2 crore and earns nothing.Regulation makes this worse. SEBI's settlement rules require brokers to return unused client funds every month or quarter, and many clients send that money straight back, often by UPI. The broker pays each time. A modest MDR here is reasonable, but a cap of Rs 5 or Rs 10 per transfer would make more sense than Rs 300. Otherwise, zero-brokerage delivery trades may not last.The credibility problemAbout 15 months ago, the Finance Ministry dismissed reports of MDR on UPI as false and baseless, and reaffirmed its commitment to free digital payments. Governments are entitled to change their minds. But this reversal joins a longer list. Online real-money gaming was treated as a game of skill, then regulated, then banned within a few years. When policy moves this way, people stop trusting assurances, and a small fee draws a large reaction.What should happen nextUPI should not be starved of funds. If it needs money for security and resilience, the Budget can provide it openly, as it would for any critical infrastructure. If the MDR stays, three safeguards would help. The government should publish what the fee collects and where it goes. It should lower the cap for capital-market transfers. And it should commit to a review after a year, using data on cash usage and bill-splitting, before any rate or threshold is raised.UPI worked because accepting a payment cost almost nothing. The October fee is small. The rules that govern it should be clear, limited and hard to change quietly.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

Between 1977 and 1990, researchers excluded three kangaroo rat species from experimental plots to see how their absence affected plants and other animals. The 13-year experiment found that two grasses became significantly more abundant in plots without the rodents that are the tall annual ‘Aristida adscensionis’ and the perennial bunchgrass Eragrostis lehmanniana. According to the research published in Oecologia titled ‘Effects of kangaroo rat exclusion on vegetation structure and plant species diversity in the Chihuahuan Desert,’ researchers indicated that reduced soil disturbance and lower predation on large seeds may have contributed to the increase in grasses.How did kangaroo rat removal affect the plantsThe researchers found that excluding the three kangaroo rat species led to clear changes in vegetation. During the 1977 to 1990 experiment, two grasses became significantly more abundant in plots where the rodents were absent. Both Aristida adscensionis, a tall annual grass, and Eragrostis lehmanniana, a perennial bunch grass, became more abundant. These vegetation changes also altered plant cover across the plots, which affected how other animals used the area. Several rodent species and foraging birds changed their use of the plots as the vegetation shifted. Together, these findings indicated that kangaroo rats played an important role in shaping both plant cover and species composition in this environment.How did researchers study the role of kangaroo rats in vegetationThe experiment examined how vegetation changed when kangaroo rats were kept out of selected plots over a long period. The exclusion ran from 1977 through 1990 and involved three kangaroo rat species. This extended period allowed researchers to track changes beyond short-term fluctuations. The study site was located in a natural transition between desert scrub and grassland, where environmental conditions and interactions among species influence vegetation. By comparing plots with kangaroo rats to those where the rodents were excluded, researchers could assess differences in plant abundance and diversity.Why did grass abundance increase after kangaroo rats were removedThe researchers proposed two linked mechanisms that may explain the vegetation changes. The first mechanism was a reduction in soil disturbance after the rodents were removed. Removing the rodents reduced soil disturbance, which may have altered conditions for plants and seeds. Their absence also meant less predation on larger seeds, which kangaroo rats normally consume. Fewer kangaroo rats feeding on larger seeds may have allowed more of these seeds to remain in the plots, thereby contributing to the increase in grass abundance. The researchers noted that these mechanisms were possible explanations, but the study did not show that either process alone caused the vegetation changes.How did different plant groups respond to kangaroo rat removalThe experiment did not affect all plant groups in the same way. Summer annual dicots had greater species diversity in plots where kangaroo rats remained present, a pattern the researchers said was consistent with predictions from keystone predator models. However, they could not determine whether this difference resulted directly from kangaroo rat activity or indirectly from the increase in grass cover after exclusion.Among winter annual dicots, the study found no experimental effect on species diversity. These contrasting results indicate that removing kangaroo rats changed some parts of the plant community, but did not lead to a uniform shift in diversity across all plant groups.Kangaroo rat removal changed how other animals used the plotsThe vegetation changes also affected other animals using the experimental plots. As grass cover increased after kangaroo rats were excluded, several other rodent species changed how they used the plots. Foraging birds responded to the altered vegetation as well. The effects of excluding kangaroo rats therefore extended beyond the plant community, changing conditions for other animals in the area. The study site was a natural transition between desert scrub and grassland, where environmental conditions and interactions among species shape vegetation structure.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1945, Oklahoma opened a nearly 4,900-foot bridge across Lake Texoma; 81 years later a record $408 million project has begun to build its replacement while the old bridge stays open
articles.summary: US News: More than eight decades after the Roosevelt Bridge first carried traffic across Lake Texoma, Oklahoma has begun work on a massive replacement project .
articles.body: More than eight decades after the Roosevelt Bridge first carried traffic across Lake Texoma, Oklahoma has begun work on a massive replacement project that will reshape one of the region’s most important transportation links. The Oklahoma Department of Transportation (ODOT) says the more than $408 million project will replace the aging US-70 bridge while keeping the existing structure open throughout construction. Details from ODOT, Equipment World and local broadcaster KXII confirm the project’s record scale, historic origins and planned 2029 completion.The US-70 Roosevelt Bridge opened in 1945, connecting Bryan and Marshall counties across Lake Texoma in southeastern Oklahoma. The original structure stretches roughly 4,900 feet and consists of 87 spans, including a distinctive Warren through-truss central span. ODOT records describe that central span as the only surviving example of its type on Oklahoma’s highway system with a polygonal top chord.Now, 81 years after its opening, the bridge is approaching the end of its useful life. An analysis found the structure at risk of becoming structurally deficient and classified it as functionally obsolete, prompting years of planning for a modern replacement.The new project represents one of Oklahoma’s largest bridge investments. The contract, valued at $408 million, was awarded to a joint venture between Zachry Construction and Traylor Bros. The project is supported by state funding and a $124 million federal Bridge Investment Program grant, which ODOT has described as the largest federal transportation grant awarded in Oklahoma for the project.The replacement will feature a new four-lane bridge across Lake Texoma, along with improvements to the US-70 approaches. The design also calls for full shoulders, improved lighting and a pedestrian path, addressing safety and capacity concerns on the existing crossing.The bridge is particularly important because US-70 serves as a regional connection between southern Oklahoma and northern Texas, supporting daily commuting, freight movement, tourism and other economic activity. Latest figures show more than 11,000 vehicles use the corridor each day.Construction is being delivered through a modified progressive design-build approach, a method being used for the first time. The process allows the transportation department and its design-build team to work together during design and construction planning, with the aim of improving the project’s schedule, design and cost efficiency.Work is already underway around the site. Crews have been clearing trees and preparing the construction area, while barges have begun drilling into the lakebed to investigate the ground conditions where the new bridge’s piers will be anchored. Lake Texoma reaches depths of about 65 feet near the existing bridge, adding another layer of engineering complexity to the project.The new bridge will be built while traffic continues to use the old one. That means drivers will not immediately lose the existing US-70 crossing as construction progresses. Once the replacement is finished, the new structure is expected to provide four lanes of modern roadway, improving reliability and safety for motorists travelling between Oklahoma and Texas.Construction is expected to continue for roughly three years, with the new bridge scheduled for completion in fall 2029. The project therefore marks more than the replacement of an aging piece of infrastructure: it represents the transition from a bridge that has served the region since the postwar era to a new crossing designed to carry traffic for decades to come.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Oh it's a she': Trump stops speech to address woman, tells her 'mother watching on TV furious'
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump paused a campaign rally in Gastonia, North Carolina, on Wednesday after a woman interrupted his speech, saying she was “goin.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump paused a campaign rally in Gastonia, North Carolina, on Wednesday after a woman interrupted his speech, saying she was “going home to mama” before resuming his remarks.Trump initially appeared to assume that the person interrupting him was a man. “Let me see his face,” he said while looking towards the disturbance, before realising the protester was a woman. “Oh, oh, it’s a ‘she.’ Hello!” he added.“She’s going home to mama — who’s watching right now. Her mother is watching right now on television, furious at the daughter,” Trump said.The exchange was captured in a video posted by Fox News from the Gastonia rally.Trump campaigns for Michael WhatleyTrump was speaking at Gastonia Municipal Airport while campaigning for Republican US Senate nominee Michael Whatley, a former chairman of the Republican National Committee who is running against former Democratic North Carolina governor Roy Cooper.The November 3 contest is for the seat being left open by Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who is not seeking re-election. Trump has backed Whatley as Republicans seek to retain the North Carolina seat.Trump also used the Gastonia rally to attack Cooper and Democrats on crime and public safety as he sought to bolster Whatley’s campaign.The Gastonia appearance was Trump’s first major campaign stop since the Republican Party’s midterm convention in Dallas last week. Trump has promised more campaign appearances ahead of the November 3 elections and urged supporters in North Carolina to treat the contest as though he were running himself, telling them to “pretend that I’m on the ballot”.Trump has used the ‘mom’ line beforeThe Gastonia exchange was not the first time Trump has responded to a rally interruption by suggesting that the protester would have to answer to their mother — before adding that the mother supported him.At a January 2020 rally in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, a protester interrupted Trump’s remarks. “Now she’s going home to mom where she will be in big trouble,” Trump said, before adding: “Because I guarantee you that mom voted for Trump.”Trump used a similar line during his 2016 presidential campaign. After a protester interrupted a rally in Erie, Pennsylvania, he told the person to “go back home to your mama” before adding: “your mother is voting for Donald Trump.”Together with the Myrtle Beach exchange last month, the earlier incidents show that Trump has returned to the same mother-themed response to protesters at rallies across different election cycles.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Sydney duo attempted 9 gigs in 12 hours; after a firefighting helicopter delay and plane propeller failure, they finished with just 15 seconds to spare
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Sydney dream pop duo Fathom recently attempted a Guinness World Records title by performing nine shows in just 12 hours across New South Wales and Can.
articles.body: Sydney dream pop duo Fathom recently attempted a Guinness World Records title by performing nine shows in just 12 hours across New South Wales and Canberra. For this, vocalist Cate Guirguis and keyboardist Jaxon Italiano travelled from Singleton to Newcastle, Gosford, Sydney, Penrith, Lithgow, Bathurst and Goulburn before reaching Canberra for their final performance.The challenge required the duo to perform at least nine shows, with each show lasting at least 15 minutes, ABC news reported. The venues also had to be at least 50 kilometres apart and located in areas with populations of more than 15,000. At least half of those areas had to have populations of 100,000 or more.Fathom used a tour bus for most of the journey, but the route also involved a helicopter, a car and a plane. They nearly failed at their goal several times because of delays during the journey. However, the duo managed to reach their final venue in Canberra and completed their 15-minute set with only 15 seconds left on the clock. "It was right down to the wire," Italiano recalled, as quoted by ABC news.Traffic and a missing helicopterThe first major delay came in Sydney. Italiano said he had expected traffic between Sydney and Penrith to be one of the biggest challenges of the day. An accident on the M4 caused delays, making the journey slower than expected.The bigger problem came after the Penrith show. Fathom had arranged a helicopter flight over the Blue Mountains to get to Lithgow. The flight was planned to help them avoid the closure of Victoria Pass. But when Guirguis and Italiano arrived at the helicopter base, their scheduled helicopter was not there."We needed to board the helicopter by 5.10 pm because they wouldn't fly after sunset. But then we got there early and there was no helicopter there," Guirguis said.They received a call from the company's head office informing them that the helicopter was being used to help extinguish bushfires in the Blue Mountains."Then we got a call back from the lady at head office, and she was saying that they were out extinguishing bushfires in the Blue Mountains, which is a fair enough excuse," Italiano said.The delay lasted about 30 minutes and Fathom eventually took the helicopter to Lithgow and continued with the next part of the challenge.Plane problem added to delayThe journey became difficult again when the duo travelled from Bathurst to Goulburn. They had arranged a chartered plane for this part of the trip, but even getting to the flight became a problem. "Firstly we went to the wrong terminal," Guirguis said.Once they were ready to leave, another problem appeared. Italiano said the plane's right propeller stopped working as they were taking off."As soon as we were taking off, the right propeller stopped working," he said. The pilot then upgraded the pair to a jet. Our pilot upgraded us to a jet which was fantastic and a lot safer," Italiano said.The problem had put the duo about an hour behind schedule. They still had to reach Canberra, set up and perform their final show before the 12-hour period ended.The final road trip went more smoothly. Guirguis said they encountered green traffic lights all the way to Canberra. "We just had green lights all the way to the venue," she said.After arriving, the pair went straight on stage and performed their final 15-minute set. "Cate and I jumped on stage, pumped out a 15-minute set," Italiano said. The countdown showed how close the attempt had become. "We had a look at the countdown, there was only about 15 seconds," he said.Fundraising for Beyond BlueThe record attempt was also linked to a fundraising effort for mental health charity Beyond Blue. Fathom said the tour had raised at least $2,200.The duo also wanted the performances to support other musicians. Italiano said half of the money from ticket sales was intended for Beyond Blue, while the other half would go to the bands supporting Fathom during the attempt."We wanted half of the sale going to Beyond Blue and the other half going to the bands that were supporting us. So we actually won't be making any profit from this," Italiano said.The pair wanted to support musicians who were struggling to find work after the Covid-19 pandemic. Italiano said, "Ever since Covid, the music industry definitely took a big hit. We found out that musicians are five times more likely to experience depression and anxiety just from the amount of stress that goes into finding work."Evidence for record being preparedFinishing the nine shows does not immediately make the attempt an official Guinness World Records achievement. Fathom now has to submit evidence so the organisation can verify the claim.The duo needs to show that at least 10 people were present at every venue through ticket links. They also needed at least two witnesses with them throughout the attempt.The band also recorded video evidence. Italiano wore a body-worn camera strapped to his chest during the journey to document the attempt.Fathom will now compile its evidence and submit the claim to Guinness World Records. The verification process could take several months.Italiano has previously gone through the record process. He broke the record for the most pull-ups in 24 hours in 2022.For now, the duo plans to take a break after completing the demanding journey. Fathom also released a song called Record Breakers on Saturday, giving the attempt its own soundtrack. "That'll be our soundtrack for the next few months," Italiano said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
